payload.title: [auth-core-8] Issuing a new reset token does not invalidate the user's prior outstanding reset tokens
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING auth-core-8 (low/correctness, confidence=medium, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/storage/password-reset-store.ts
LINES: 34-56

WHAT: issue() always INSERTs a new token row and never marks any previously-issued, still-valid tokens for the same user as consumed/expired. Multiple unconsumed reset tokens for one account can therefore be live simultaneously (up to the 60-minute TTL). If a user requests several resets (or an attacker who briefly observed one link triggers another), an older leaked-but-unused token remains valid alongside the newest one, widening the window for misuse. Best practice is single-outstanding-token-per-user.

IMPACT: Larger window of valid reset tokens per account than necessary; a previously-observed token stays usable even after the user requests a fresh one.

SUGGESTED FIX: In issue(), within a transaction, mark all prior unconsumed tokens for (tenantId, userId) as consumed/expired before inserting the new one (or DELETE them), so only the most recent token verifies.
